## 4062.T — IBIDEN CO LTD | Daily-chart timing overlay (3–6 month horizon)

**Data note:** prices are vendor-sourced daily bars in JPY; the exchange suffix `.T` implies Tokyo, but exchange/timezone and adjustment basis were not supplied. One anomalous bar exists — 2026-07-31 prints O=H=L=C=8,325 on 2.13M shares (single-price session), which can distort averages slightly. The 12-month series (2,235.3 on 2025-10-01 → 8,045 now) is a ~5x move; I cannot independently verify split adjustment, so absolute levels are used as reported. No corporate-action-adjusted series was available for cross-check.

### 1. Technical conclusion
The three-to-six-month technical condition is **damaged, still in a downtrend, with no confirmed stabilization**. 4062.T has fallen 35.1% from its 2026-10-06 closing high of 12,400 to 8,045 on 2026-11-02, is 20.9% below its 50-day SMA (10,168.07) and 10.9% below its 10-day EMA (9,026.10). The one thing holding the long-term structure together is the 200-day SMA at 7,779.40: the 2026-11-02 low of 7,695 traded 1.1% beneath it, and the close recovered 3.4% above it. That is a single-session recovery, not a base. Principal caveat: much of the decline has occurred through two violent down-gaps, which is characteristic of news-driven re-pricing; technical timing signals are least reliable in that regime.

### 2. Evidence
- **Trend (10 EMA / 50 SMA / 200 SMA).** Short and medium trend are bearish and averages are rolling over; the 50 SMA at 10,168.07 sits only 30.7% above the 200 SMA, so the bullish long-term alignment is intact but compressing. Price made a lower high on 2026-10-29 (intraday 10,280, close 9,859) and then lost 15.2% in one session to 8,359 on 2026-10-30. These three averages are one correlated trend cluster, not three votes.
- **Momentum.** RSI 37.20 is weak but not oversold; it peaked at 66.7 on 2026-10-06. MACD −542.01 vs signal −389.88, histogram −152.14, i.e. re-widening negative after a brief improvement (−88.6 on 10-29). A two-point RSI non-confirmation exists (price lower low 8,045 vs 8,248 on 10-26; RSI 37.2 vs 33.3) but is too thin to call a divergence signal.
- **Participation.** VWMA (20d) 9,125.99 is 13.4% above the 8,045 price, meaning recent turnover has occurred at materially higher prices — a descriptive measure of overhead supply, not proof of who is selling. 2026-11-02 volume (29.47M) was well above the ~10–20M norm of early October.
- **Volatility.** ATR 820.40 = 10.2% of price. Daily ranges of 8–12% mean any tight risk point is inside normal noise.
- **Conflicting evidence.** The 200 SMA is still rising steeply, price closed back above it, and 2026-11-02 closed in the upper half of its range (low 7,695, close 8,045) on heavy volume — the only constructive observation in the tape.

### 3. Decision levels

| Zone | Basis | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| 9,786–10,495 | Unfilled 2026-10-15 gap; 50 SMA 10,168 / Bollinger mid 9,938 inside | Major repair zone; a close back inside would neutralize the October breakdown |
| 8,622–9,859 | Unfilled 2026-10-30 gap | Overhead vacuum/supply; the trend is still down while price is below it |
| 9,026–9,126 | 10 EMA / VWMA | First meaningful trend-repair trigger on a closing basis |
| 8,598 | 2026-10-22 close (prior support) | Minimum "selling exhausted" marker |
| 7,695–7,779 | 2026-11-02 low / 200 SMA | Pivotal; a decisive close below shifts the long-term trend question from "intact" to "in doubt" |
| 6,735–7,430 | July 2026 lows (closes 6,735–7,430) | Next reference shelf if the 200 SMA fails |

### 4. Conditional outlook
**Primary trigger (heuristic, unvalidated):** a daily close above the 9,026–9,126 area, held for more than one session, would establish that the post-October downtrend has at least stopped making lower highs; MACD histogram turning positive would be supporting, not mandatory, confirmation. Invalidation of that repair attempt: rejection back below 8,598, or any close below 7,695.

**Weakening condition:** a close below 7,695 with follow-through would put the 6,735–7,430 July shelf in play and mark the first break of the 200 SMA in this advance. Note the trade-off: waiting for 9,026 confirmation costs roughly 12% of entry price versus acting at current levels.

### 5. Investment implication
Technically, this is not a favorable chart for initiating or adding exposure: trend, momentum and volume-weighted price are all aligned lower, and the only support is a rising 200 SMA being tested for the first time. That is a *timing* judgment only. Nothing here addresses whether IBIDEN's business is attractively valued, and this analysis neither supports nor changes any fundamental target price. Given ATR of ~10% of price and two unfilled gaps, position sizing should be materially smaller than for a normal-volatility name, and stop orders should not be treated as gap protection.

*This is a daily-chart timing overlay on a 3–6 month investment horizon, not a standalone trading recommendation; no position size, cost basis, or mandate was supplied.*

# Fundamental Analysis: 4062.T

## 1. Executive conclusion

**Fundamental rating: Neutral.** Decision horizon: 3–6 months (to ~end-April 2027).

- **Business direction: strongly positive.** 4062.T (Ibiden Co., Ltd.) is the leading domestic supplier of high-performance IC package substrates, and the operating evidence in the latest half is unambiguous: H1 FY3/27 (six months to 30 Sep 2026) revenue rose 34.3% to JPY262,546m and operating profit rose 84.6% to JPY60,116m, both first-half records, with the Electronics segment contributing JPY50,028m of segment profit at a 29.0% margin [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1, p.12].
- **Earnings direction: positive but decelerating in rate of change.** FY3/27 guidance is revenue [[565.0]] and operating profit [[133.0]], i.e. +35.8% and +114.4% [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3]. The second half therefore requires only a modest step-up from H1 (implied H2 operating margin 24.1% vs H1 22.9%) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Forecast versus guidance:** the model's FY3/27 equals guidance by construction (H1 actual plus H2 guidance). For FY3/28 the model is [[190.0]] operating profit versus company guidance of JPY165.0bn, because the model reverses the roughly JPY10bn price-decline buffer management has embedded and assumes stronger Cell 8 ramp, mix and utilisation.
- **Forecast versus consensus:** the model's FY3/28 operating profit of [[190.0]] is identical to the consensus figure cited by Citi [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. **The base case provides no material forecast edge versus the available consensus for this metric.**
- **Cash-flow quality: weak on a normalised basis.** H1 operating cash flow of JPY193,178m was flattered by a JPY118,796m increase in advances received; excluding that, operating cash flow was roughly JPY74bn against H1 capex of JPY48.9bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9, p.10]. Capex is guided to ~JPY200bn in FY3/27 and ~JPY350bn in FY3/28, so normalised free cash flow is negative through the forecast period [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Balance-sheet condition: strong.** Net cash of roughly JPY258bn at 30 Sep 2026 (cash and deposits JPY420,487m less interest-bearing debt of ~JPY162bn), equity ratio 53.5% [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1, p.4, p.5].
- **Valuation conclusion: full.** At [[JPY 8,045]] the stock trades on [[35.9x]] FY3/28 EPS of [[224.1]] and roughly 15–16x FY3/28 EV/EBITDA, with negative normalised free cash flow and a 0.25% dividend yield. The model's fair-value range of [[6,274]]–[[8,515]] brackets the price, but the price sits in the upper third of that range.
- **Main catalyst (within horizon):** a formal Cell 7 / Cell 9 investment decision with customer-backed terms, promised within FY3/27 (i.e. by March 2027), and/or a revised FY3/31 plan [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].
- **Main risk:** the market has begun to price a share-loss narrative as a third AI-GPU substrate supplier enters, and the Q2 briefing itself was a negative catalyst — the shares fell sharply on the results and briefing [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].
- **Principal limitation:** no peer multiples, no historical valuation series and no revenue/net-profit consensus are available in the corpus; the FY3/28 consensus reference is a single operating-profit figure.

---

## 2. Company and earnings structure

**How 4062.T makes money.** Three reportable segments. In H1 FY3/27:

| Segment | H1 FY3/27 sales (JPY m) | Segment profit (JPY m) | Margin | H1 FY3/26 margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Electronics | 172,540 | 50,028 | 29.0% | 22.4% |
| Ceramics | 46,156 | 5,391 | 11.7% | 9.7% |
| Others | 43,849 | 4,623 | 10.5% | 7.7% |
| Consolidated | 262,546 | 60,116 | 22.9% | 16.7% |

Source: [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.11, p.12]. Electronics supplied 83% of consolidated segment profit.

- **Electronics** is the valuation driver: high-performance IC package substrates built on semi-additive process (SAP) for AI GPUs, AI ASICs, server CPUs, high-end switches and EMIB/EMIB-T bridge packages [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12, p.14]. Revenue is volume × area × layer count × price; the company's own framing is that substrate *area* demand grows far faster than unit demand — from CY26 to CY30, AI GPU/ASIC units grow 1.8x but SAP area demand grows 5.4x, and server CPU units 1.3x versus 2.5x area [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12].
- **Ceramics** is automotive and industrial: DPF/AFP for internal combustion, EV products, and graphite/FGM for nuclear power [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.15]. It is a low-growth, cyclical ballast business; management guides H2 Ceramics operating income of only JPY2.1bn on automotive sluggishness [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Others** includes the intersegment-heavy businesses (intersegment transfers of JPY16,828m in H1) and is not a valuation driver.

**Concentration and competitive position.** Customer concentration is high and rising by implication: the AI GPU substrate market is described as moving from a two-player structure (4062.T plus one Taiwanese supplier) to three with a Korean entrant, and the company states Tier-1 is "currently being monopolised" [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1; doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Barriers are real but not absolute: qualification cycles, yield on high-layer-count SAP, and — per management — *support engineers* rather than buildings or money, which is why a greenfield decision today takes a minimum of four years to mass production [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**Key operating variables:** (i) qualified high-end capacity and its utilisation; (ii) substrate area/layer mix; (iii) ASP and the pace of contractual price-downs; (iv) yield, especially on EMIB-T; (v) depreciation from the Cell 6/Cell 8 build-out; (vi) customer prepayments, which fund the build.

---

## 3. Latest results and operating drivers

**Company-confirmed facts (H1 FY3/27, six months to 30 Sep 2026):**

- Net sales JPY262,546m (+34.3% YoY); operating profit JPY60,116m (+84.6%); ordinary profit JPY61,009m (+88.9%); profit attributable to owners of parent JPY38,574m (+74.8%) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1].
- Gross profit JPY97,705m on cost of sales JPY164,840m → gross margin 37.2%, versus 34.7% in H1 FY3/26 (JPY67,913m / JPY195,485m). SG&A rose only 6.4% to JPY37,589m, so SG&A fell from 18.1% to 14.3% of sales [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7]. **This is the mechanical source of the margin expansion: gross-margin gain plus sharp operating leverage on a fixed cost base.**
- Basic EPS JPY68.63, diluted JPY65.10, restated for the two 2-for-1 splits (1 Jan 2026 and 1 Oct 2026) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1].
- Extraordinary loss of JPY1,650m, driven by a JPY1,606m loss on retirement of non-current assets, partly offset by JPY813m subsidy income [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].
- Effective tax rate 34.5% (JPY20,490m on pretax JPY59,358m) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].

**Management's stated drivers:** "favorable pricing and exceptionally strong demand for AI-related products" in Electronics; Ceramics slightly ahead of plan on DPF backup parts [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**Analyst interpretation (not company disclosure):** Q2 standalone (H1 less Q1) was revenue [[139.3]] and operating profit [[33.2]], a 23.8% margin versus Q1's 21.8% ([[123.2]] / [[26.9]]). The sequential incremental operating margin was therefore about 39% — (33.2−26.9)/(139.3−123.2) — which is the single most important number in the release: it says incremental premium substrate revenue converts at close to 40 cents on the dollar before depreciation step-up. That is consistent with a genuinely tight market rather than a one-off price spike.

**What did not happen, and matters:** no Cell 7 or Cell 9 investment was announced, and the medium-term plan revision was small. JPM described the FY3/27-onward figures as "half-hearted" and attributed the sharp share-price fall to the scale of the plan revision and the absence of a Cell 7/Cell 9 announcement [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. Citi called the outlook "below market expectations" and "negative" [same source].

---

## 4. Management guidance and expectations

**FY3/27 guidance (company disclosure, revised upward):** net sales [[565.0]], operating income [[133.0]], ordinary income [[134.5]], profit attributable to owners of parent [[89.0]], EPS [[157.2]] [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3]. Implied H2: revenue [[302.5]], operating profit [[72.9]], net profit [[50.4]] [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**FY3/28 (company's "FY2027") medium-term plan:** revenue JPY650.0bn, operating profit raised from JPY150.0bn to JPY165.0bn, with the Electronics operating margin assumption raised from 29% to 31% [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1; doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Management explicitly confirmed the plan still embeds the same price-decline assumption as before, which GS estimates at roughly JPY10bn of operating-profit drag [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].

**FY3/31 (company's "FY2030"):** revenue JPY1.0tn, operating profit JPY300bn+, maintained unchanged. This target excludes the newly announced JPY151bn Cell 6 expansion, excludes use of spare Cell 8 space, and excludes Cell 7/Cell 9 [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1; doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**Consensus:** the only external consensus figure in the corpus is FY3/28 operating profit of JPY190bn, cited by Citi as the level below which management's JPY165bn guidance sits [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. Revenue, net profit and EPS consensus are not stated anywhere in the corpus — a genuine data gap, not evidence of mispricing.

**Conflicts and data-quality issues I could not reconcile:**

1. **FY3/28 guidance of JPY165bn vs JPY163bn.** Citi, GS and the earnings-call transcript all say JPY165bn; the JPM summary in the same broker note says group-wide operating profit was "revised this time to ¥650.0bn / ¥163.0bn" [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. I treat JPY165bn as the company figure (three corroborating sources) and flag JPY163bn as a transcription error in the internal note.
2. **The JPM summary contains several internally inconsistent figures** and should not be relied on numerically: it attributes "FY2026 cumulative group-wide revenue of ¥665.0bn / operating profit of ¥133.0bn" (665 is the FY3/28 revenue level, not FY3/27), states FY2026 depreciation of "¥3.1bn" (the transcript and model say [[81.0]]), states FY2030 group revenue of "¥100.0bn" (the target is JPY1.0tn), and gives SAP demand of "13.5 for FY2027 (YoY +3.5%)" against "11.2bn for FY2026" — which is +20.5%, not +3.5% [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. I use the transcript and presentation for these items.
3. **Cell 6 product description conflicts across company documents.** The presentation labels the Cell 6 output "High-Performance IC Package Substrate for AI ASIC" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13]; the tanshin says "for CPUs" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.14]; the call and SMBC say it is EMIB-related for CPU, not EMIB-T [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call; doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. The investment amount is also stated as JPY150bn in the presentation and JPY151bn in the tanshin and call. These are disclosure inconsistencies, not economically material, but they reduce confidence in the segment-level detail.
4. **Capex for FY3/27: ~JPY200bn (transcript) vs JPY210bn (JPM).** I use ~JPY200bn, the management figure [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

---

## 5. Independent forecast

I adopt the verified model's annual path, which I have checked against the filings and which I regard as economically defensible, with the caveats noted in Section 7.

| JPY bn | FY3/26A | FY3/27E | FY3/28E | FY3/29E |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | [[416.2]] | [[565.0]] | [[665.0]] | [[780.0]] |
| Operating profit | [[62.0]] | [[133.0]] | [[190.0]] | [[225.0]] |
| Operating margin | [[14.9]]% | [[23.5]]% | [[28.6]]% | [[28.8]]% |
| Net profit | [[63.7]] | [[89.0]] | [[126.9]] | [[150.7]] |
| EPS, full share (JPY) | [[112.5]] | [[157.2]] | [[224.1]] | [[266.1]] |

**Key assumptions and their basis:**

- **FY3/27 = H1 actual + H2 guidance.** [[262.5]] + [[302.5]] = [[565.0]] revenue; [[60.1]] + [[72.9]] = [[133.0]] operating profit; [[38.6]] + [[50.4]] = [[89.0]] net profit. This is not an independent forecast — it is arithmetic on guidance. My own view is that a modest beat is more likely than a miss, because H2 guidance implies a 24.1% margin against Q2's already-delivered 23.8% and against management's own description of extremely tight supply-demand [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. A range of JPY133–140bn operating profit is defensible; I do not have evidence to justify a point estimate above guidance, so I do not publish one.
- **FY3/28 above guidance, at consensus.** The bridge is: base [[133.0]] + [[60.0]] incremental margin on [[100.0]] of higher advanced-substrate revenue at roughly 60% incremental margin − [[10.0]] price declines − [[9.0]] depreciation increase ([[90.0]] less [[81.0]]) + [[16]] cost reduction and operating leverage = [[190.0]]. The 60% incremental margin is the load-bearing assumption. It is supported by the observed ~39% sequential incremental margin in Q2 and by the fact that incremental revenue is almost entirely premium Electronics; it is *not* supported by any company disclosure of incremental margin, and it is the assumption I would attack first.
- **FY3/29** adds Cell 8 fuller loading and initial Cell 6 contribution, with [[20]] of depreciation increase and [[15]] of price erosion. Cell 6 operations begin sequentially from FY2029 (company's FY2029 = year to March 2030), so only a small contribution is assumed — correctly, since a ramp start is not full-run-rate revenue [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13].
- **Tax:** 30% assumed for FY3/28, 32% for FY3/29, against 34.5% actually incurred in H1 FY3/27 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7]. The lower forward rate is an assumption, not guidance, and is mildly flattering to net profit.

**Quarterly build (FY3/27):** Q1 [[123.2]]/[[26.9]]/[[17.9]]; Q2 [[139.3]]/[[33.2]]/[[20.7]]; Q3 [[145.2]]/[[32.8]]/[[20.2]]; Q4 [[157.3]]/[[40.1]]/[[30.2]]. Q1 and Q2 are reported. The Q3/Q4 split is a model assumption (48/52 revenue, 45/55 operating profit, 40/60 net profit), not guidance. **I flag one internal awkwardness:** the implied Q3 operating margin of 22.6% is *below* Q2's 23.8%, which sits uneasily with management's back-end-weighted and improving-mix commentary. The internal note instead models Q3 operating profit of JPY36.5bn at 24.5% [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast]. I treat the model's Q3 as conservative rather than wrong, and note that the full-year total is unaffected.

---

## 6. Forecast bridges

**Revenue, FY3/27 → FY3/28 (base [[565.0]] → [[665.0]]):**

| Driver | JPY bn | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Cell 8 ramp and advanced substrate volume | +[[80]] | Derived; Cell 8 (JPY280bn, AI GPU substrates) starts sequentially from FY2027 = FY3/28 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13] |
| AI GPU/ASIC area growth and mix | +[[30]] | Derived; SAP demand index 100 in CY26 → 350 in CY30 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12] |
| Product price declines | −[[10]] | Guidance; broker estimate of management's embedded assumption [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1] |
| **Total** | **[[665.0]]** | |

No double count: Cell 8 volume and area growth are separated because Cell 8 is *new qualified capacity* while area growth applies to *existing* capacity. The residual is zero, which is itself a warning sign — a bridge that closes exactly is a constructed bridge, not an observed one.

**Operating profit, FY3/27 → FY3/28 (base [[133.0]] → [[190.0]]):**

| Driver | JPY bn | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Incremental margin on higher revenue | +[[60]] | Derived; [[100.0]] revenue × ~60% incremental operating margin |
| Product price declines | −[[10]] | Guidance [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1] |
| Depreciation increase | −[[9]] | Guidance; [[90.0]] FY3/28 less [[81.0]] FY3/27 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call] |
| Cost reduction and operating leverage | +[[16]] | **Analyst assumption — residual.** Not independently supported as an operating driver. |
| **Total** | **[[190.0]]** | |

The [[16]] residual is 8% of the forecast operating profit and is disclosed as a residual, not presented as a business driver. Note also that the depreciation drag is small ([[9]]) precisely because management confirms much of the Cell 6/Cell 8 spend remains in construction in progress through FY3/27 — construction in progress was JPY126,192m at 30 Sep 2026, up JPY14,399m in six months [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.4]. **The depreciation cliff is therefore deferred, not avoided:** management guides EBITDA margin above 50% and toward 60% by FY3/28–FY3/30, which mathematically requires depreciation to rise much faster than sales thereafter [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**Net profit, FY3/27 → FY3/28 (base [[89.0]] → [[126.9]]):** +[[39.9]] after-tax operating profit increase ([[57.0]] × (1 − 30%)) − [[2]] non-operating and minority adjustment = [[126.9]]. The [[2]] is an assumption.

**A note on the FY3/26 base.** FY3/26 net profit of [[63.7]] *exceeded* operating profit of [[62.0]]. The vendor cash-flow statement shows a gain on investment securities of JPY40.3bn in the year to 31 Mar 2026, alongside JPY57.5bn of investment sales and a fall in investment securities from JPY58,797m to JPY32,285m [vendor cash-flow and balance-sheet data, 2026-11-02]. **FY3/26 net profit therefore contains a large non-recurring investment gain.** The consequence is that the guided +39.7% net profit growth for FY3/27 materially understates underlying earnings growth: on my calculation, stripping the after-tax investment gain would put FY3/26 underlying net profit near JPY35–36bn, making FY3/27's [[89.0]] roughly a 2.5x increase. This is an analyst calculation, not a company figure, and it is the single most important adjustment a reader should make to the headline growth rates.

---

## 7. Consensus and variant perception

**Where the forecast differs:**

| Metric | Period | Guidance | Consensus | Model | Variance vs consensus |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operating profit | FY3/28 | JPY165.0bn | JPY190.0bn | [[190.0]] | 0.0% |

**Why the model differs from guidance:** the model reverses the roughly JPY10bn price-decline buffer management has deliberately retained, and assumes stronger Cell 8 contribution, richer mix and higher utilisation than the company's 31% Electronics margin assumption [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].

**Why the model does not differ from consensus:** because the consensus reference *is* JPY190bn. **The base case does not currently provide a material forecast edge versus the available consensus for this metric.** I will not manufacture one.

**Where an edge could instead come from — and whether the evidence supports it:**

- **Timing of the Cell 7/Cell 9 decision.** Management committed to decide and disclose within FY3/27, i.e. by March 2027 — inside the horizon. Citi names this as the next catalyst [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. This is a genuine event risk in both directions, not a forecast edge.
- **Duration of growth beyond FY3/28.** The FY3/31 target of JPY300bn+ operating profit excludes Cell 6 (JPY151bn), spare Cell 8 space, and Cell 7/9. Management states Cell 6 alone is "pure upside" to the FY3/30 target, with revenue roughly 1x the investment at a >30% margin [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. That is real optionality — but it lands in FY3/30 and beyond, outside a 3–6 month horizon.
- **Cash-flow quality.** No edge: the model and the company both show negative normalised free cash flow.
- **Valuation.** This is where the debate actually sits, and it is a derating argument, not an earnings argument.

**Evidence that would confirm the above-consensus view:** Q3 operating profit at or above ~JPY36bn with Electronics margin above 30%; a further FY3/27 guidance raise; a Cell 7/9 announcement on customer-backed terms.

**Evidence that would invalidate it:** Q3 margin below Q2's 23.8%; any indication that the Korean entrant is taking AI-GPU allocation rather than only incremental demand; Cell 8 qualification slipping a quarter; EMIB-T mass production slipping from H2 FY3/28.

---

## 8. Cash flow and balance sheet

**Operating cash flow quality is the weakest part of the story.** H1 operating cash flow was JPY193,178m, but this includes a JPY118,796m increase in advances received [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9]. **Interpretation of the advances.** Advances received rose from JPY80,950m at 31 Mar 2026 to JPY199,746m at 30 Sep 2026 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.5]. The evidence supports the *positive* reading of this signal: the increase coincides with customer-requested capacity commitments (Cell 6 allocated to CPU/EMIB at customer request; Cell 7/9 under negotiation with customers), not with cancellations or renegotiated terms [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. It reduces funding and stranded-capacity risk. It does **not** prove permanent pricing power, and it must not be treated as recurring organic cash generation.

**Capex and free cash flow.** H1 purchases of PP&E were only JPY48,310m plus JPY560m of intangibles [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.10] — against a full-year plan of ~JPY200bn. **Roughly three-quarters of FY3/27 capex is therefore back-end loaded into H2**, which is both an execution risk and a reason the H1 free-cash-flow picture looks better than the full-year will. On my arithmetic: FY3/27 EBITDA of ~JPY214bn ([[133.0]] + [[81.0]]) less ~JPY45bn tax less ~JPY200bn capex implies normalised free cash flow of roughly −JPY30bn; FY3/28 with EBITDA of ~JPY280bn ([[190.0]] + [[90.0]]) less ~JPY57bn tax less ~JPY350bn capex implies roughly −JPY125bn. These are my calculations, not model figures.

**Balance sheet.** Cash and deposits JPY420,487m; interest-bearing debt of ~JPY162bn (current bonds JPY10,000m, bonds payable JPY35,000m, convertible bonds JPY56,036m, long-term loans JPY61,000m, leases JPY50m) → **net cash of roughly JPY258bn** [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.4, p.5]. ## 9. Valuation

**Method selection.** P/E on FY3/28 EPS and EV/EBITDA are the appropriate primary methods: the company is profitable, capital-intensive and in a capacity-build phase, so P/E captures the earnings trajectory while EV/EBITDA neutralises the very different depreciation profiles across the build cycle. FCF yield is included as a discipline check, not as a primary method, because free cash flow is negative by design during the build. DCF is not used: the corpus does not provide a defensible cost of capital, and the terminal value would be dominated by assumptions about capacity beyond FY3/31 that management has not yet decided.

**P/E.** At [[JPY 8,045]] and FY3/28 EPS of [[224.1]] on the full-share count, the multiple is [[35.9x]]. The model's fair-value range of [[6,274]]–[[8,515]] corresponds to 28.0x–38.0x that EPS, with a midpoint of ~33x. **The current price sits in the upper third of the fair-value range.** The multiple is defensible only if FY3/28 is a trough year for the multiple — i.e. if EPS keeps compounding at the FY3/29 rate of [[266.1]] (+18.8%) and beyond.

**EV/EBITDA.** FY3/28 EBITDA on the model is ~JPY280bn ([[190.0]] + [[90.0]]). Market capitalisation is JPY4,564.6bn (Bloomberg, 567.4m shares at [[JPY 8,045]]). Against net cash of ~JPY258bn, EV is ~JPY4,306bn → **~15.4x**. If net cash falls to ~JPY89bn after the cumulative capex outflow, EV is ~JPY4,476bn → **~16.0x**. For a capital-intensive manufacturer with negative normalised free cash flow, 15–16x is full, though not extreme given the growth rate.

**FCF yield.** Negative on a normalised basis in both FY3/27 and FY3/28 (Section 8). There is no free-cash-flow support for the valuation.

**Dividend yield.** 0.25%. No support.

## 10. Catalysts within the decision horizon

1. **Q3 FY3/27 results (late January / early February 2027).** The first read on whether the H2 step-up is real. Watch Electronics margin versus the 29.0% H1 level and versus the ~30% management targets for H2.

4. **Evidence on the third AI-GPU substrate supplier.** Any confirmation that the Korean entrant is taking incremental demand rather than share would remove the derating pressure; the opposite would compound it.

## 11. Risks and invalidation conditions

**Business risk.** A third AI-GPU substrate supplier entering a two-player market. Management argues total industry capacity will still fall far short of demand and that no meaningful share loss is expected [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call], but Citi explicitly warns that "the resulting decline in market share poses a risk of a temporary stock price correction" [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. **Forecast risk.** The 60% incremental-margin assumption in the FY3/28 bridge is the single largest unverified input. **Execution risk.** Cell 8 must ramp sequentially through FY3/28. A one-quarter slip in Cell 8 hits revenue and depreciation absorption simultaneously.

**Cash-flow and funding risk.** Capex of ~JPY200bn in FY3/27 and ~JPY350bn in FY3/28 against negative normalised free cash flow. The company is funding this from cash, customer advances and debt capacity. Net cash of ~JPY258bn is comfortable for one year of this, not for three. **Valuation risk.** 35.9x FY3/28 EPS with negative FCF and a 0.25% yield leaves little protection. The model's bear case of [[4,945]] (−39%) is not a remote tail given 96.9% realised volatility.

**Regulatory / geopolitical risk.** Not evidenced in the corpus beyond generic FX exposure. The internal note flags a yen materially stronger than ¥145/US$ as a translation risk but states the materials do not permit a reliable per-yen sensitivity [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast]. **Thesis invalidation conditions (observable):**
- Q3 FY3/27 operating profit below ~JPY33bn or Electronics margin below 28%.
- Cell 8 first revenue slipping beyond H1 FY3/28.
- A Cell 7/9 announcement at materially worse investment efficiency than Cell 6/Cell 8 (i.e. revenue multiple below 1x or margin below 30%).
- Evidence of actual AI-GPU allocation loss, not just a new entrant's announcement.
- FY3/28 operating profit tracking below JPY165bn guidance.

**Rating**: Underweight

**Decision horizon:** 3–6 months (to ~end-April 2027).

## 1. Executive conclusion

- **Rating:** Underweight. Action is to reduce exposure and put no new money to work at current levels; this is not a bearish call on Ibiden’s franchise.
- **Fundamental view:** Operating momentum is genuinely strong — H1 FY3/27 revenue rose 34.3% and operating profit 84.6%, with Electronics margin at 29.0% [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1, p.12]. But the forecast offers no material edge: FY3/27 model revenue [[565.0]], operating profit [[133.0]] and net profit [[89.0]] equal guidance by construction, and FY3/28 model operating profit [[190.0]] equals the only cited consensus figure of JPY190.0bn. Valuation is full and normalised cash conversion is weak.
- **Technical timing:** Damaged. 4062.T is 20.9% below its 50-day SMA, below its 10-day EMA, and only one session recovered above a pierced 200-day SMA. The tape argues against adding; it does not change fundamental value.
- **Valuation range:** Model fair value [[6,274]]–[[8,515]]; at [[JPY 8,045]] the stock sits in the upper third. Upside to the top is ~5.8%, downside to the bottom ~22% (my arithmetic).
- **Main catalyst:** Q3 FY3/27 results, then the promised Cell 7/Cell 9 investment decision and/or revised FY3/31 plan by March 2027.
- **Main risk:** The third AI-GPU substrate supplier share-loss narrative compresses the multiple before shipments move; the FY3/28 bridge also depends on an undisclosed [[60]]% incremental margin and a [[16]] residual.

## 2. Investment thesis

1. **No forecast edge.** FY3/27 is H1 actual plus H2 guidance: [[262.5]] + [[302.5]] = [[565.0]] revenue, [[60.1]] + [[72.9]] = [[133.0]] operating profit, [[38.6]] + [[50.4]] = [[89.0]] net profit. FY3/28 operating profit [[190.0]] matches consensus of JPY190.0bn. The model is precise, not differentiated.
2. **The FY3/28 bridge is the weak point.** It converts a [[100.0]] revenue increase at roughly [[60]]% incremental margin and includes a [[16]] cost-reduction/leverage residual. Observed Q2 sequential incremental margin was ~39%. At ~45%, FY3/28 operating profit would be ~JPY175bn — above company guidance of JPY165.0bn but below consensus, removing the base-case edge.
3. **Valuation and cash flow provide little support.** At [[JPY 8,045]], the stock trades on [[35.9]]x FY3/28 EPS of [[224.1]], with negative normalised free cash flow through FY3/28 and a 0.25% dividend yield. H1 operating cash flow of JPY193,178m included JPY118,796m of customer advances; ex-advances it was roughly JPY74bn against H1 capex of JPY48.9bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9, p.10].

## 3. What is already priced in

The market appears to price continued AI substrate area growth, the Cell 8 ramp, and above-guidance FY3/28 delivery — consensus operating profit of JPY190.0bn sits well above company guidance of JPY165.0bn. It has also begun to price the third-supplier share-loss narrative after the Q2 briefing and the absence of a Cell 7/Cell 9 announcement; the shares fell sharply on the results and briefing [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. - **Guidance vs model:** FY3/27 model revenue [[565.0]], operating profit [[133.0]] and net profit [[89.0]] match guidance with 0.0% variance because the build is H1 actual plus H2 guidance. This is arithmetic on guidance, not an independent forecast.
- **Model vs guidance for FY3/28:** Model revenue [[665.0]] and operating profit [[190.0]] sit above company guidance of JPY650.0bn revenue and JPY165.0bn operating profit. - **Model vs consensus:** FY3/28 operating profit [[190.0]] is identical to the Citi-cited consensus of JPY190.0bn. **There is no material forecast edge versus consensus for the only available consensus metric.**
- **Key assumptions:** The [[60]]% incremental margin and [[16]] residual are the load-bearing inputs. The Q3/Q4 split is an assumption, not guidance; the model uses a lower forward tax rate than the 34.5% incurred in H1 FY3/27; share-count bases differ between market cap and EPS. Revenue, net-profit and EPS consensus are not available in the corpus — a genuine data gap.

## 5. Valuation and cash flow

- **Valuation:** Fair-value range [[6,274]]–[[8,515]], based on 28–38x FY3/28 EPS of [[224.1]]. At [[JPY 8,045]] the multiple is [[35.9]]x and EV/EBITDA is roughly 15–16x. The price is in the upper third of the range.
- **Scenario skew:** Bear [[4,945]] (−39%), base [[8,000]] (−1%), bull [[9,530]] (+18%). No probabilities are assigned; the distribution is negatively skewed and the base case is roughly flat to the current price.
- **Cash flow:** Normalised free cash flow is negative through FY3/28. FY3/27 capex is guided near JPY200bn and FY3/28 near JPY350bn; customer advances fund part of this but are not recurring operating cash flow. Net cash of roughly JPY258bn and a 53.5% equity ratio are strengths, but they do not make the equity cheap. Convertible dilution is ongoing — 5.1m new shares were issued in October, with JPY56bn remaining.

## 6. Technical timing

The technical structure weakens timing. 4062.T is in a downtrend, 20.9% below its 50-day SMA at 10,168 and below its 10-day EMA at 9,026. The 200-day SMA at 7,779 was pierced, with a low of 7,695, and the close recovered only 3.4% above it for one session — the overlay itself calls this “a single-session recovery, not a base.” Overhead gaps at 8,622–9,859 and 9,786–10,495 remain supply. ATR is 10.2% of price and realised volatility is 96.9%, so tight stops are unreliable and gap risk runs both ways. This is a timing overlay only; it does not alter the fundamental fair-value range.

## 7. Catalysts within the decision horizon

1. **Q3 FY3/27 results** (late January/early February 2027): watch operating profit versus the model’s [[32.8]], Electronics margin versus 29.0% in H1, and sequential incremental margin versus Q2’s ~39%.
2. **Cell 7/Cell 9 investment decision by March 2027:** a customer-backed announcement with disclosed terms would be the cleanest positive catalyst.
3. **Revised FY3/31 plan:** management has said it will revisit the JPY300bn+ target once the capex programme is finalised; an upward revision would help.
4. **Third-supplier evidence:** confirmation that the Korean entrant is absorbing incremental demand rather than taking AI-GPU allocation would remove derating pressure.
5. **Convertible conversion flow:** a persistent EPS headwind, not a positive catalyst.

Not in the horizon: EMIB-T mass production in H2 FY3/28, Cell 6 operations from FY2029, and Cell 7/9 mass production from FY2031 onward.

- **Share-loss narrative:** the multiple can compress on the narrative before any shipment is lost; Citi explicitly flags this risk.
- **Forecast risk:** if incremental margin is ~45% rather than [[60]]%, FY3/28 operating profit falls to ~JPY175bn, below consensus. The [[16]] residual is not an independently supported driver.
- **Execution risk:** Cell 8 must ramp through FY3/28; equipment lead times are long and support-engineer availability is the binding constraint.
- **Cash-flow/funding risk:** negative normalised free cash flow through FY3/28; additional Cell 7/9 commitments would extend the funding requirement.
- **Valuation risk:** [[35.9]]x FY3/28 EPS with negative normalised FCF and a 0.25% yield leaves little protection; the bear case is −39%.
- **Fundamental invalidation:** Q3 operating profit below ~JPY33bn or Electronics margin below 28%; Cell 8 first revenue slipping beyond H1 FY3/28; FY3/28 tracking below company guidance of JPY165.0bn; actual AI-GPU allocation loss; Cell 7/9 terms materially worse than Cell 6/Cell 8 economics. A break below 7,695 with follow-through is a technical contingency, not by itself fundamental evidence.

- **Existing holders:** reduce exposure and put no new money to work at current levels.
